A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TARFLOW and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Relocated material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original TARFLOW likelihood and generation results, architectural and sampling ablations, and generated images on ImageNet and AFHQ.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a larger-model result and comparisons with volume-preserving and channel-coupling controls.

M1.justification: The TARFLOW transformations, objective, noise augmentation, denoising, and guidance procedures are unchanged. Unconditional guidance moves to Appendix B. The new architectural variants are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional ImageNet 64x64 likelihood and generation, conditional ImageNet 64x64 and 128x128 generation, and conditional AFHQ 256x256 generation. The additions use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Section 3.6 and Table 5 add volume-preserving and channel-coupling baselines evaluated against TARFLOW. Comparator membership in the existing likelihood and FID benchmark tables remains unchanged, including the unconditional comparison relocated to Appendix Table 6.

E3.justification: The added conditional ImageNet 64x64 model uses 1024 channels, batch size 768, and 320 epochs, versus 768 channels, batch size 256, and 200 epochs for v1's best model. The new architectural controls use Gaussian noise 0.05 and guidance weights 0 and 2. Existing benchmark evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an architectural ablation testing non-volume-preserving transformations against a volume-preserving control and autoregression against channel coupling. Existing noise, denoising, guidance, depth-scaling, and sampling-trajectory analyses are retained, including material moved to the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and comparisons using fixed initial noise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds FID 2.66 for the wider 2-1024-8-8 model while retaining 2.90 for 2-768-8-8; this is an additional configuration, not a same-setting improvement. New Table 5 reports architectural-control results, including guidance-2 FIDs of 5.7, 51.0, and 20.4 for TARFLOW, VP, and channel coupling. Figure 6 additionally specifies FID 267 for the existing single-block failure.

T1.justification: The flow definitions, Jacobian and loss derivations, Tweedie-based denoising, and guidance equations remain unchanged. Equation 11 is relocated to Appendix B; no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about TARFLOW, sub-3 BPD likelihood, noise augmentation, denoising, guidance, and competitive generation. Additional experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 2.5 newly interprets successful denoising as evidence that learning the noisy density can recover its score using TARFLOW alone. Section 3.6 explains the VP control's sampling failure through small latent magnitudes, motivating a learned prior variance. Existing inference limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 7 documents the added model's training configuration, including 32 GPUs versus eight for the previous best conditional ImageNet 64x64 model. Section 3.6 describes control construction and the VP prior adjustment. Existing code access, precision, hardware type, KV-cache implementation, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands the description of Flow++ and explicitly discusses Flow Matching, while removing context and citations concerning iResNet, flow-enhanced VAEs, and likelihood training of diffusion models, including Behrmann et al. (2019) and Lu et al. (2022). Core positioning remains; two broader survey subsections move to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The document substantially reorganizes the main-text/appendix boundary: unconditional guidance moves to Appendix B, broader related work to Appendix A, and trajectory analysis to Appendix D.1. Related-work prose is condensed, experimental introductions are shortened, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is extensively rearranged: benchmark tables are regrouped, unconditional FID and qualitative guidance/trajectory displays move to the appendix, and Figure 4 changes from side-by-side to vertically stacked panels. A new ablation table is added and Figure 11(b)'s incomplete caption is corrected. Existing sample images are retained.

improvement.justification: The new architectural controls provide direct evidence for design choices that v1 did not test, and the larger-model result adds documented scaling evidence. These modestly strengthen the paper while preserving its original results. The controls are only briefly specified and some related-work context is removed, limiting the overall gain.
